extracted.intended_audience: Members of the public and affected agencies (stakeholders) invited to comment on CDC's Paperwork Reduction Act information collection
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and notice for submitting public comments on CDC's proposed Generic Information Collection Request (ICR) for traveler risk assessment and management during disease outbreaks, including what OMB is particularly interested in and procedural submission requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity and practical utility of the collection
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether the proposed collection of information is necessary for the proper performance of the functions of the agency, including whether the information will have practical utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OMB is particularly interested in comments that (a) evaluate whether the proposed collection of information is necessary for the proper performance of the functions of the agency, including whether the information will have practical utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy of burden estimate and validity of methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the accuracy of the agency's estimate of the burden of the proposed collection of information, including the validity of the methodology and assumptions used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OMB requests comments that (b) evaluate the accuracy of the agencies estimate of the burden of the proposed collection of information, including the validity of the methodology and assumptions used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhance quality, utility, and clarity of information
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide suggestions to enhance the quality, utility, and clarity of the information to be collected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OMB is interested in comments that (c) enhance the quality, utility, and clarity of the information to be collected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize respondent burden and use of technology
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify ways to minimize the burden of the collection on respondents, including use of appropriate automated, electronic, mechanical, or other technological collection techniques or other forms of information technology, e.g., permitting electronic submission of responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OMB requests comments that (d) minimize the burden of the collection of information on those who are to respond, including, through the use of appropriate automated, electronic, mechanical, or other technological collection techniques or other forms of information technology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of information collection costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the costs associated with the proposed information collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OMB is particularly interested in comments that (e) assess information collection costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural requirement: comment submission timeline and methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide written comments and recommendations within 30 days of notice publication to specified channels (www.reginfo.gov; attention CDC Desk Officer at OMB; fax).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments and recommendations for the proposed information collection should be sent within 30 days of publication of this notice to www.reginfo.gov/public/do/PRAMain. Direct written comments and/or suggestions regarding the items contained in this notice to the Attention: CDC Desk Officer, Office of Management and Budget, 725 17th Street NW, Washington, DC 20503 or by fax to (202) 395-5806. Provide written comments within 30 days of notice publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural option: request for additional information / obtain ICR materials
rubrics_metrics.description: To request additional information on the proposed project or to obtain a copy of the information collection plan and instruments, contact CDC via the provided telephone number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To request additional information on the proposed project or to obtain a copy of the information collection plan and instruments, call (404) 639-7570.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal/regulatory authorization for collection
rubrics_metrics.description: Information collection and traveler screening authority must be consistent with statutory and regulatory bases cited (e.g., Section 361 of the PHS Act 42 U.S.C. 264; 42 CFR 71.20; 42 CFR 71.4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice cites legal authority: Section 361 of the Public Health Service (PHS) Act (42 U.S.C. 264) and 42 CFR 71.20; CDC's authority for collecting certain passenger and crew data is in 42 CFR 71.4. Collections should be within these authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of Generic ICR — topics to be encompassed
rubrics_metrics.description: The Generic ICR is expected to encompass data collection related to entry screening of travelers, public health risk assessment, post-arrival management, health department follow-up, traveler surveys, and evaluation activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DGMH anticipates that this Generic ICR would encompass data collection related to: entry screening of travelers and (if indicated) public health risk assessment conducted either in person or virtually; post-arrival management of travelers as specified in CDC recommendations for travelers arriving from outbreak areas; Health Department of jurisdiction follow up of indicated travelers; surveys of travelers to determine the most efficient channels for reaching travelers and refine public health messaging for travelers coming from the outbreak area; evaluation of entry screening, post-arrival management, and Health Department follow-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design guidance: flexibility and rapid implementation of instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: Data collection instruments and methods must be able to be rapidly created and implemented and remain flexible because specific questions will change or new questions will evolve with each disease outbreak.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because disease outbreaks do not occur at regular intervals and each response is unique, instruments and methods must be rapidly created and implemented to direct appropriate public health action; often specific questions will change, or new questions will evolve with each disease outbreak.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational requirement for airline-provided data
rubrics_metrics.description: Under an interim final rule and Order, airlines must collect and transmit certain passenger and crew data to CDC within 24 hours of an order or retain for 30 days and transmit upon request; this data collection (contact information) is already approved under OMB Control No. 0920-1354.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under the IFR, airlines must transmit these data to CDC within 24 hours of an order. The Order requiring the collection of this information was issued on October 25, 2021,... airlines may transmit the required information using existing data-sharing infrastructure in place between the airlines and DHS or they must retain the information for 30 days and transmit it to CDC within 24 hours upon request. This information collection for contact information is already approved under OMB Control No. 0920-1354.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden estimate reporting format and components
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide estimated annualized burden hours broken down by respondent type, form name, number of respondents, responses per respondent, and average burden per response (hours).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice presents an 'Estimated Annualized Burden Hours' table with columns: Type of respondents, Form name, Number of respondents, Number of responses per respondent, Average burden per response (in hours). CDC requests OMB approval for an estimated 10,559 annual burden hours and provides a row-level breakdown by form and respondent type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation component: surveys and response evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Include surveys of travelers to determine efficient communication channels and response surveys to evaluate the screening and monitoring processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Planned data collections include 'SAMPLE VHF Response Survey of Travelers' and surveys to determine the most efficient channels for reaching travelers and refine public health messaging; evaluation of entry screening, post-arrival management, and Health Department follow-up is expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdictional monitoring burden on State/Local Health Departments
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate and account for the burden on state and local health departments for traveler monitoring and follow-up, including number of jurisdictions, frequency, and average time per response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The burden table includes rows for 'CDC SAMPLE VHF Jurisdiction Traveler Monitoring' and 'CDC SAMPLE VHF Jurisdiction Final Survey' with specified numbers (e.g., 70 jurisdictions, 104 responses, 5/60 hours average burden), indicating expectations to estimate jurisdictional burden.
